candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items), within Physiological Integrity; this item tests supportive respiratory-care positioning and secretion-management measures tailored to client comfort and tolerance.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Supportive airway-clearance positioning and comfort-focused respiratory care
candidate.educational_objective: Describe postural drainage as individualized, gravity-assisted positioning that mobilizes retained secretions toward larger airways and may be combined with percussion, vibration, breathing, and coughing techniques when clinically appropriate.

options.A: The client is positioned so gravity can help move secretions from targeted lung regions toward larger airways; manual percussion or vibration may be added when appropriate
options.B: The client remains in one neutral position because body position has no relationship to the lung region being drained
options.C: Coughing is suppressed during and after treatment so mobilized secretions remain in the smaller airways
options.D: Postural drainage is a universal routine treatment for every respiratory condition regardless of secretion retention, tolerance, or contraindications

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/StatPearls guidance describes postural drainage as positioning the body to use gravity to move mucus from specific lung regions toward larger airways. Manual chest physiotherapy can include percussion and vibration to loosen and mobilize retained secretions, and coughing or deep breathing may be used to help expel mobilized mucus. B ignores the segment-specific role of positioning. C is opposite to the goal of secretion clearance. D is incorrect because airway-clearance techniques require individualized selection based on secretion burden, clinical condition, tolerance, and contraindications.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current NCBI/StatPearls content directly supports gravity-based segmental positioning, optional manual percussion/vibration, and cough/breathing maneuvers as components of individualized secretion-clearance therapy.
candidate.source_locator: NCBI Bookshelf 'Postural Drainage and Vibration' → Introduction: postural drainage positions the body to use gravity to drain mucus from specific lung areas; vibration applies rhythmic pressure to loosen mucus. Technique or Treatment → Manual Chest Physiotherapy: percussion loosens/mobilizes mucus; different positions facilitate drainage from different lung segments; gravity assists movement toward larger airways; deep breathing and coughing may help expel loosened secretions. Contraindications/Indications: technique selection is individualized and should account for clinical status and contraindications.
candidate.source_version_date: StatPearls; last update 2024-06-08; current 2026 NCBI Bookshelf edition accessed 2026-08-18
candidate.stem: A client with retained respiratory secretions is receiving postural drainage as part of an individualized airway-clearance plan. Which description of the technique is accurate?
